clue.text: Obtain cash for dress

parts.note: to obtain something is to get it
ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Someone takes out money to pay for a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a garment, but it is the verb: to dress, as soldiers dress ranks, is to make ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress, in the old sense of preparing or arranging, is to make preparations.

clue.text: Kind of football field that made a martyr of Lawrence

definitions.text: that made a martyr of Lawrence

explanation.surface: A sports pitch is linked to the death of a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football the field is nicknamed after its grid of lines; St Lawrence was martyred by being roasted on an iron grill of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: An American football pitch is nicknamed for its lines, and the grill on which St Lawrence was roasted is the same word.

clue.text: Flunkey has to take notice — the consumer's coming

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
one who consumes food is an eater

explanation.surface: A servant must pay attention because the diner is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady or sycophant was once called by this fuller name, from the quack's servant who pretended to eat toads.

clue.text: Worker leaves animal to bolt

indicators.note: the worker departs from the animal, so its letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: an antelope is an animal
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee walks away from a beast, which then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes ANT out of ANTELOPE, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly to marry is to bolt, or abscond, with a lover.

clue.text: Gray's prospect of Eton was so remote

definitions.text: Gray's prospect of Eton was so

explanation.surface: A poet's view of a famous school was far off.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote 'Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College'; Eton is the English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's ode title supplies the adjective for the view, and that adjective also means far away or aloof.

clue.text: For tots a divine mouthful

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or clergyman
a sup is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Children are given a holy sip of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' reads as small children, but it is the verb: to tot up a column of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot is to total a set of figures, which is the phrasal verb here.

clue.text: Fancy, yacht, perhaps, becoming an object of infatuation

parts.note: a fancy is a dream or daydream
a yacht is one example of a boat, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Imagining a sailing vessel turns into an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: A very attractive person whom others swoon over is the idiomatic sense here.

clue.text: Tony's sale-room is lively

parts.note: the possessive s of Tony is taken just as it is written
a mart is a market or sale-room

explanation.surface: A man named Tony's auction house is a busy place.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony is not a name but the adjective tony, meaning stylish; 'is lively' adds a second sense, since a smart pace is a brisk one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony is slang for stylish or fashionable, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Wages plot in hospital?

parts.note: wages are pay
a plot of garden ground is a bed

explanation.surface: Someone schemes about salaries while lying in a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'plot' too: a bed in a British NHS hospital for which a private patient pays.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a private patient could pay for a reserved bed in an NHS ward.

clue.text: Moulding Canadian province would need Avon's previous backing

indicators.note: the province would need another piece to be complete, so that piece is removed to leave this

parts.note: Nova Scotia is a province of Canada

indicators.note: the river name stands before the rest and is turned backwards

parts.note: the Avon is a British river, taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of decoration from Canada would need something from the Avon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AVON into NOVA, which 'previous' puts in front; taking NOVA from NOVA SCOTIA leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave moulding at the base of a column carries this architectural name.

clue.text: I had a little house in the Rockies

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
ho is an abbreviation of house

explanation.surface: Someone recalls owning a small cabin in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state lying in the Rocky Mountains, so it sits there as a location.

clue.text: Clerical worker conveys hush-hush material by a landline

parts.note: something hush-hush is secret
RY, railway, is a line over land

explanation.surface: An office worker carries classified documents along a telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landline' suggests a telephone, but it is a railway line across land.
explanation.definitionFit: An office assistant handling letters and records is a clerical worker.

clue.text: Crude (not as supplied by OPEC)

parts.note: crude in the sense of coarse or unrefined manners, not the crude oil that oil-exporting nations sell

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, clumsy or lacking refinement is the sense of crude meant here, as opposed to oil.

clue.text: Joint in which top churchmen may be seen

definitions.text: in which top churchmen may be seen

explanation.surface: A woodworking joint where senior clergy appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner joint in carpentry has this name, as does the tall pointed headdress of bishops.

clue.text: There's no clear evidence of anything being taken thus

definitions.text: There's no clear evidence of anything being taken thus

parts.words: There's no clear evidence of anything being taken thus
parts.note: a thing accepted without proof is accepted on faith alone

explanation.definitionFit: Accepting something without proof, relying on belief in the teller, is the idiom here.

clue.text: Cover-up lost her new order

indicators.note: the letters are placed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A scandal is hushed up after she lost a fresh command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' looks like one word, but 'Cover' is the definition and 'up' starts the fodder; 'new order' rearranges UP LOST HER.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a chair or sofa with padding and fabric is to cover it.

clue.text: Clears an empty space at Spithead

parts.note: an, the indefinite article, gives A
a void is an empty space
read as Spit head: the head, or first letter, of Spit

explanation.surface: A naval anchorage off Portsmouth has some open water.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is the stretch of sea off Portsmouth, England; read as Spit's head it gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler clears a fence by steering free of it, keeping away from contact.

clue.text: Turns up record bowling spells

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
in cricket an over is a spell of six balls from one bowler

explanation.surface: A recording reveals periods of cricket bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up something is to find or unearth it.

clue.text: Gave in when put on ice

explanation.surface: Someone yielded when a plan was shelved.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to another's judgment is deferring to them, and putting a plan on ice is postponing it.

clue.text: Sign as member of famous family

explanation.surface: An autograph proves membership of a celebrated clan.
explanation.walkthrough: Sagittarius, the zodiac sign, is the bowman; The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius is depicted as a bowman, and the radio soap's farming clan bears this surname.

clue.text: Stranger able to hold his drink

explanation.surface: An odd fellow can take his liquor well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'able to hold his drink' sounds like a hardy drinker, but it describes a large drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means odd, so its comparative is stranger; a large goblet for wine is also called this.

clue.text: Aims set out by French artist

indicators.note: the letters are put out of place, set out afresh

explanation.surface: A painter from France lays out his goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AIMS SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: Soppy girl left in college, I hear

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sentimental young woman stayed at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'college, I hear' adds a second hint: Magdalen College, Oxford, is pronounced the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearfully sentimental, like the weeping Mary Magdalene, is soppy.

clue.text: Russian capital supplies second boat

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: The city provides a backup vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city and seat of government of Russia.

clue.text: Refuse the old king a pound

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for his dyke
L, from libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch turns down a quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun: rubbish, waste parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails and trimmings of a butchered carcass are waste, the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Basket liable to give way

explanation.surface: A wicker container is likely to break.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush basket for figs carries this old name, and something weak and fragile is apt to give way.

clue.text: Mickey-taker from Cornish village?

parts.note: Mickey is a mouse, so the place where one is taken is its burrow in the skirting, also a village name in Cornwall

explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish fishing village bears the same name as a small gap a rodent uses.

clue.text: See a distressed daughter comforted

indicators.note: distress the letters, so they are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at an upset girl who was then soothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges SEE A into EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or worry is to soothe or comfort.

clue.text: Make good list of records from Winnie's house

parts.note: the chart lists best-selling records
well means good, in good health

explanation.surface: Someone restores a playlist from Churchill's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie is Winston Churchill, whose Kent home bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's country home in Kent, now a National Trust property.

clue.text: Guide for viewer going round square

indicators.note: the viewer encircles the next piece, which sits inside

parts.note: a seer is one who sees
a T-square, so T

explanation.surface: An instructor for a spectator walks around a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts T inside SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct or pilot a course.

clue.text: They can be heard howling from Australian mounts

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: those howling are wailers

explanation.surface: Australian horses are heard crying out.
explanation.walkthrough: Walers are horses from New South Wales, used as cavalry mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses bred in New South Wales were used as cavalry mounts.

clue.text: Treated to a coat when all's said and done, maybe

indicators.note: the letters may be put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is given a coat after all is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges SAID and DONE; 'when all's' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal given a protective oxide coat by electrolysis is coated, or treated.
